_about: Attack-surface model for the threat-modeling showcase, v2. Nodes and links follow data/architectures/G-CONV.json, G-D53.json and transparent.json; the transparent architecture follows 3GPP TR 38.821 and shares the TT&C, update, ATLO and GNSS links of G-CONV (source graph only: no TT&C, update or ATLO link to the G-D53 feeder satellite). Additions are marked basis 'assumed'. Entry paths are computed by phalanx.tm from the attach rules below; nothing per architecture is hand-listed. Analyst-drafted, unreviewed.

trust_boundaries._about: Paper trust boundaries (ASIANComNet 2026 manuscript, §III-D and Table I; data/rules/vocabulary.json paper_boundaries) per link id, as in the source architectures' figure_alias. Labels only: no rule gates a step on them.

defs.TB2: 지상 ↔ 우주 (feeder 링크, TT&C 명령 경로)

TC-UL.basis: stated: source E-TCUL, Fig. 2 (TR52 crosses TB2 on the TT&C command path)

SLE.basis: interpretation: source E-SLE, Table I places TT&C/SOC (SLE-SDL) at TB2

NG.basis: interpretation: source E-NG, feeder link (TB2) then ground core (TB3)

ATLO.basis: none: source E-ATLO, physical custody is not a paper boundary

F1-ISL.basis: none: source E-F1, inter-satellite link; no paper boundary covers it

HOST.basis: none: on-board hosted RAN ↔ bus; no paper boundary covers it

HOST-F.basis: none: on-board hosted RAN ↔ bus; no paper boundary covers it

GNSS-sat_service.basis: none: GNSS reception; no paper boundary covers it

GNSS-sat_feeder.basis: none: GNSS reception; no paper boundary covers it

partner connection.basis: none: partner → mission operator; not a paper boundary

proximity.basis: none: physical proximity; not a paper boundary

FEEDER.basis: interpretation: transparent feeder link (ground ↔ space), as the G-CONV feeder in this label set

sdls.label: SDLS authentication + anti-replay on the TC uplink
sdls.source: CCSDS 355.0-B-2; use on the uplink not stated by any pinned source
sdls.note: authentication and anti-replay only; SDLS encryption is optional and not assumed

ipsec_f1.label: IPsec on F1 over the inter-satellite link
ipsec_f1.source: TS 33.501 §9.8 (mandatory to implement, use optional); D5.3 design

as_security.label: 5G access-stratum / NAS security (UE ↔ gNB; also covers Uu relayed over a transparent feeder link)

segregation.label: Segregation of the hosted RAN from the satellite bus
segregation.source: assumed; ENISA TR07 names its absence as an enabling condition

vectors.ground: attacker acts from inside the mission's own ground systems (operations centre, ground station, update pipeline; insider)
vectors.rf_link: attacker transmits or receives on the TT&C radio link from equipment outside the mission
vectors.feeder_rf: attacker transmits or receives on the feeder link that carries Ng between the gateway and the satellite RAN (rogue gateway)
vectors.user_terminal: attacker acts from a user terminal on the service link (rogue or compromised UE, service-link jamming or eavesdropping)
vectors.supply_chain: attacker acts through hardware, software, updates or integration before or outside operations
vectors.trusted_party: attacker rides a connection the mission already trusts: partner, vendor remote access
vectors.crosslink: attacker reaches a satellite from another satellite over an inter-satellite link
vectors.proximity: attacker acts from a spacecraft or weapon close to the satellite, or with physical access
vectors.hosted_payload: attacker controls a function hosted on the satellite but run by another operator (the on-board RAN run by the mobile network operator) and uses it as a door into the host bus

ground.label: Compromised own ground system / insider
ground.credential_note: mission_valid: compromised operations centre or insider holding mission keys; none: attacker inside the ground segment without the mission keys, e.g. a ground-station front end (SDLS keys assumed held at the operations centre)

rf_link.label: External transmitter on the TT&C link (rogue ground station)

feeder_rf.label: Rogue gateway on the feeder link

user_terminal.label: User terminal on the service link
user_terminal.credential_note: subscriber_valid: a legitimate subscriber turned attacker or a compromised UE; none: a rogue terminal

trusted_party.label: Trusted partner / vendor remote access
trusted_party.label_ko: 신뢰 관계 파트너 / 벤더 원격 접근
trusted_party.credential_note: partner_valid: the partner's own access to the operations centre, not mission command keys

crosslink.label: Compromised neighbour satellite
crosslink.credential_note: mno_valid: the neighbour's RAN holds the F1 security association

proximity.label: Proximity spacecraft / counterspace weapon / physical access
proximity.label_ko: 근접 우주선 / 대우주 무기 / 물리적 접근

door._about: Crossing from a hosted RAN function into its host bus needs a kept door technique; without it the chain stops at the RAN function.

step_authority._about: Authority needed by non-entry steps (from the TR52 pilot profiles, data/rules/techniques.json; children inherit from their parent). tc: the step sends telecommands, so it needs a path over a tc_uplink and, when SDLS is on, mission keys. credential: the step uses a mission-valid credential.

link_only._about: Techniques that act on a radio link itself without the spacecraft accepting a command, with the link kinds they act on. For origins that attack links they need only such a link on the path (an attacker inside a ground station counts for the TT&C link). A link-only outcome also needs an accepted link-only action. A mapping row may override with link_only true/false and a reason.

G-CONV.label: Conventional: full gNB on one service satellite
G-CONV.label_ko: 기존형: 서비스 위성 한 대에 gNB 전체 탑재

ue.label: User terminal
ue.basis: assumed: added for the service-link origin (analyst decision)

sat_service.gnb.label: gNB hosted on the service satellite
sat_service.gnb.basis: assumed: RAN run by the mobile network operator, bus by the mission operator; the source file has one mission-operator satellite node

gnss.label: GNSS signals in space
gnss.basis: assumed: every bus has a GNSS receiver (SPARTA EX-0014.04/EX-0016.03 describe it)

links.label: service link (Uu)
links.basis: assumed: added with the user terminal

links.label: hosted RAN ↔ bus interface
links.basis: assumed: the hosted RAN needs power, time and data from the bus (SPARTA IA-0006 describes this interface)

G-D53.label: D5.3 split: DU on the service satellite, CU on the feeder satellite, F1 over the inter-satellite link
G-D53.label_ko: D5.3 분할형: DU는 서비스 위성, CU는 feeder 위성, F1은 위성 간 링크(ISL)

sat_service.du.label: DU hosted on the service satellite

sat_feeder.cu.label: CU hosted on the feeder satellite

gnss.label: GNSS signals in space
gnss.basis: assumed: every bus has a GNSS receiver (SPARTA EX-0014.04/EX-0016.03 describe it)

transparent.label: Transparent: gNB on the ground, satellite relays Uu (3GPP Rel-17/18 baseline)
transparent.label_ko: 투명 중계형: gNB는 지상, 위성은 Uu를 중계

gnb.label: gNB / NTN gateway on the ground
gnb.basis: 3GPP TR 38.821 transparent payload: the gNB is on the ground and the satellite relays the radio signal

sat_service.payload.label: Transparent payload (radio relay)
sat_service.payload.basis: 3GPP TR 38.821: the transparent payload relays Uu between the service and feeder links and runs no RAN function; operated by the satellite operator, assumed here to be the mission operator. No payload ↔ bus attack link is modelled: the relay is not a RAN interface

gnss.label: GNSS signals in space
gnss.basis: assumed: every bus has a GNSS receiver (SPARTA EX-0014.04/EX-0016.03 describe it)

links.label: Ng (terrestrial)
links.basis: 3GPP TR 38.821: Ng stays terrestrial in the transparent architecture; NDS/IP per TS 33.210 as in G-CONV

links.label: feeder link (relayed Uu)
links.basis: 3GPP TR 38.821: the feeder link carries the relayed Uu between the gateway/gNB and the payload; the payload performs no authentication itself, but 5G AS security between the UE and the ground gNB (TS 33.501) protects the relayed traffic end to end

links.label: service link (Uu, relayed)
links.basis: assumed: as G-CONV; Uu is relayed by the payload and terminates at the gNB on the ground, where 5G AS/NAS security also terminates (TS 33.501)

reverse_door._about: From a compromised bus into the RAN function hosted on it (SPARTA IA-0013, the inverse of IA-0006). When kept and accepted, the RAN functions on the reached bus are recorded as reached.

ground_side._about: Techniques that act in ground systems or supplier sites: they need an accepted entry, not the satellite bus.

capture._about: Techniques that read traffic off a link. They fail on an encrypting link whose control is on, unless the attacker's credential bypasses it.
